name: Trinity College and the Book of Kells
blurb: Georgian university campus with the old Long Room library and the illuminated Book of Kells, Dublin's most famous manuscript.
priceText: Adults €26, conc €21 (students and seniors, valid student card), child €14-20

name: National Gallery of Ireland
blurb: Free national gallery of Irish and European art; the Turner watercolours only go on show in January, so not in December.

name: Kilmainham Gaol
blurb: Former prison (1796-1924) where the leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising were executed; a sobering stop for Irish history.

name: National Museum of Ireland - Archaeology
blurb: Free museum with the Treasury: the 12th-century Ardagh Chalice, the Tara Brooch and striking prehistoric gold jewellery.

name: Gallagher's Boxty House
blurb: Traditional Irish classics: boxty, the potato pancake rolled around fillings, plus a good stew and chowder in a small, friendly room.

name: Elephant & Castle
blurb: Original outlet of the popular chain, famous for its chicken wings; expect a wait for a table at Saturday lunchtime.

name: Dublin Literary Pub Crawl
blurb: Two-hour pub crawl mixing street theatre, Irish literature and history with pub stops; a lively, cheap way to meet people.

name: The Workman's Club
blurb: Former working men's club turned live music venue: a 300-capacity main room, a relaxed bar and a friendly crowd.

name: Guinness Storehouse
blurb: Self-guided tour of Guinness brewing history in the St James's Gate storehouse; a classic Dublin outing, though not cheap.

name: Glasnevin Cemetery tour
blurb: Guided tour of Glasnevin, a Catholic cemetery opened in 1832 and packed with Irish history; a thoughtful, atmospheric walk.

name: Musée du Louvre
blurb: Enormous museum spanning ancient Egypt, Greece and Rome, medieval Europe and Napoleonic France; pick a few wings, not all of it.
priceText: €22 for EEA residents/nationals, €32 for others; EEA nationals aged 18-25 free with photo ID

name: Musée d'Orsay
blurb: Former 1900 railway station with a rich Impressionist and Post-Impressionist collection; the great hall alone is worth the visit.
priceText: €9; concessions €6.50; under 18 or 26 for EU member states free

name: Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris
blurb: Free city collection of modern art from World War I onwards, in the east wing of the Palais de Tokyo; temporary shows charge extra.
priceText: Free; temporary exhibitions have various charges

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
blurb: Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité; entry is free, but booking ahead saves a long queue.
priceText: Free; booking recommended as queues can be long

name: Marché d'Aligre
blurb: Paris's cheapest open-air market with produce, clothes and antiques; the covered Beauvau market and food shops are next door.

name: Chez Marianne
blurb: Pletzl institution: falafel sandwiches from the walk-up window for a few euros, plus a sit-down room with cheap vegetarian menus.
priceText: Falafel out of the window €4; dining room about €15 for a vegetarian menu, up to €22 à la carte

name: Le Piano Vache
blurb: Long-running student bar in the Latin Quarter, walls covered in band posters and regulars' passport photos; cheap beer.

name: Nouveau Casino et Café Charbon
blurb: Downstairs bar and upstairs dance hall in Oberkampf that rocks until dawn; a favourite with young Parisians after other places close.

name: Canal Saint-Martin promenade
blurb: Leisurely stroll along the canal with cafés and pastry stops; a cheap way to feel local, with lovely sunsets.

name: Public swimming pool and ice rink, La Défense
blurb: Public pool complex in the La Défense business district with a winter ice rink; no price or hours are listed, so check first.

name: Fourvière basilica
blurb: White-marble hilltop basilica dedicated to the Virgin Mary, patron of Lyon; free to enter and a classic landmark above Vieux Lyon.

name: Saint-Jean Cathedral
blurb: Primatial cathedral of Vieux Lyon, built between 1180 and 1480; free to visit, but dress appropriately as it is a working church.

name: Musées Gadagne
blurb: Renaissance palace with Lyon's city history and the Guignol puppet museum; under-26s go free and two museums are good value.
priceText: One museum €6 incl. audioguide; two museums €8; under 26 and disabled free

name: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon
blurb: Large fine-arts museum in the Palais Saint-Pierre with a strong collection of European paintings and sculpture; a good rainy-day pick.
priceText: €6, reduced €4, under 18, EU students and some others free
when: Wed-Mon 10:00-18:00 (Fri from 10:30); closed Tue and public holidays

name: Croix-Rousse market
blurb: Popular local food market on the Croix-Rousse hill with many producers; Sundays are crowded, but the neighbourhood mood is the draw.

name: Brasserie Georges
blurb: Cavernous traditional brasserie serving Lyonnaise classics and Alsatian choucroute, a generous pile of sauerkraut and sausages.

name: Ninkasi
blurb: Lyon institution with its own brewery, a free-entry Kafé room for electronic shows and the Kao hall for rock; great for a night out.

name: Hot Club de Lyon
blurb: Jazz club since 1948 in an old cellar, with live jazz most nights of the week; an intimate way to hear local musicians.

name: Jardin des Curiosités
blurb: Small surreal garden hidden behind a metal door at the bottom of a car park, with a good viewpoint over southern Lyon.

name: Parc de la Tête d'Or
blurb: One of France's largest urban parks: an English-style garden with lakes, greenhouses and a zoo; free and lovely for a winter walk.

name: Colline du Château
blurb: Hilltop park with the ruins of an old castle and a spectacular free viewpoint over the Baie des Anges and the harbour.

name: Musée Marc Chagall
blurb: Stained-glass windows and large Chagall paintings in a Cimiez museum; a must-see even for people who don't follow art.
priceText: Full €8, reduced €6; free for students below 26 and on the first Sunday of the month

name: Musée Matisse
blurb: Matisse paintings, drawings and sculptures in a 17th-century Genoese villa in Cimiez; a compact, charming collection.
priceText: Full €10; groups of 10+ €8; students and under-18s free with proof of eligibility

name: Musée des Arts Asiatiques
blurb: Free Asian art museum in a striking building beside a lake, with Indian, Chinese and Southeast Asian works and world art.

name: Lou Pilha Leva
blurb: Old Town counter spot serving socca, Nice's chickpea flatbread, at a very low price; order at the counter and eat it on the go.

name: Flower Market (Marché aux Fleurs)
blurb: Old Town street market that began as a flower market; now mostly produce, bakes and souvenirs, and open on Sunday mornings.

name: Ma Nolan's
blurb: Irish pub next to the opera in Old Town with live music every night, sport on four screens and good food.

name: Le Blue Whales
blurb: Rock-leaning pub since 1993 with live music, sport on screen, Wednesday trivia at 20:00 and pub grub; lively late.

name: Cliff Walk (Sentier Littoral)
blurb: Coastal path around Cap de Nice toward Villefranche; expect several hundred steps, but it is free and used mostly by locals.

name: Parc Phoenix
blurb: Botanical garden with about 2,500 plant species, a tropical glasshouse and some animals; a warm break on a grey winter day.
priceText: €5.20; ages 12-18 €3; under 12 free; Nice museums pass-holders €3

name: Vieux-Port
blurb: Historic harbour where fishermen sell their catch by auction; free to stroll, and best seen in the evening light over the boats.

name: Basilique Notre-Dame de la Garde
blurb: Hilltop basilica hung with model boats left by fishermen, with one of the best views over the city and harbour.

name: Mucem (Musée des Civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée)
blurb: First national French museum outside Paris: a modern dark-box building linked by footbridges to an old fort; big shows.

name: FRAC Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
blurb: Contemporary art collection in a striking building by Kengo Kuma; a cheap stop, with a reduced rate for under-25s and students.

name: Four des Navettes
blurb: Bakery famous for the navette, a dry boat-shaped biscuit and Marseille speciality; its recipe has stayed secret for nearly a century.

name: Marché de la Plaine (Place Jean-Jaurès)
blurb: Local food market on Place Jean-Jaurès, called La Plaine; arrive early for the best produce and the best deals.

name: Le Trolleybus
blurb: Cave-like club with three rooms: chart hits in one, underground techno and house in another; a reliable late night out.

name: Polikarpov
blurb: Lively late bar with an outside terrace and a wide cocktail list; one of the cheaper places in town for a beer.

name: Calanques between Marseille and La Ciotat
blurb: Fjord-like limestone coves popular for hiking, sport climbing and diving; a good winter outing when the weather is fine.

name: Parc Borély
blurb: Large park around the Château Borély, about 300 m from the sea; a good siesta spot before a sunset drink at the beach-side bars.

name: Grossmünster
blurb: Old Romanesque church where reformer Zwingli was appointed priest in 1519; the steep tower climb gives a great view over Zurich.

name: Kunsthaus Zürich
blurb: Zurich's main art museum, strong on Swiss painters such as Hodler and sculptor Giacometti, plus major international works.
priceText: Fr. 16/11 for the permanent collection; free on Wednesdays

name: Landesmuseum Zürich (Swiss National Museum)
blurb: Swiss National Museum with history, archaeology and art across the ages; the best single overview of how Switzerland got here.
priceText: Adults CHF 13; concessions CHF 10 (incl. students); children up to 16 free

name: Zoological Museum of the University of Zurich
blurb: Free university collection: local fauna on the first floor and animals from around the world below; quiet, quirky and budget-friendly.

name: Zeughauskeller
blurb: Historic 1487 guild hall serving hearty sausages, stews and rösti in a Brauhaus setting; touristy, but the portions are big and good.

name: Globus Bellevue food hall
blurb: Food-focused Globus store near Stadelhofen with a large ground-floor eatery serving fusion dishes; handy for a quick bite.

name: Helsinki
blurb: Small bar-club with live concerts most nights and an outdoor area in summer; a home for independent acts from across Switzerland.

name: Gonzo
blurb: Basement club, mostly not electronic; long queues and a strict door, but Wednesday hip-hop and Thursday student nights are fun.

name: Uetliberg
blurb: Hill above Zurich with a 360-degree tower view; hike up, or take the S10 from the main station in about 20 minutes.
priceText: Tower CHF 2.50; train covered by a ZVV ticket or Zürich Card

name: Zoo Zürich
blurb: Zoo with the big Masoala Rainforest Hall, an indoor tropical environment that suits a cold December day.

name: Cathedral Saint-Pierre and its towers
blurb: Former Catholic cathedral where Calvin preached; climb the towers for city views. The combined ticket adds the Reformation museum.
priceText: Towers CHF 7; students/apprentices aged 17-25 CHF 5 with valid card; combined Espace Saint-Pierre ticket CHF 18

name: International Museum of the Reformation
blurb: Museum in Maison Mallet beside the cathedral: rare books, manuscripts and objects tracing the Reformation; cheap for students.
priceText: Adult Fr. 10; students aged 16-25 Fr. 7; children 7-16 and groups Fr. 5

name: CERN Science Gateway
blurb: Free, mostly hands-on museum on CERN's particle physics and quantum science, presented in five languages; a good rainy-day stop.

name: Jet d'Eau
blurb: Geneva's landmark fountain, pumping water about 140 m into the air over Lake Geneva; free to see.

name: Buvette des Bains
blurb: Lakeside spot in the middle of the lake: beach in summer, fondue restaurant in winter, and a cheap plat du jour all day.

name: Edward's sandwiches
blurb: Packed sandwich and cake café where locals queue for warm sandwiches at lunch; cheap and filling, but seats are hard to find.

name: Le Ferblanterie
blurb: Grungy student bar on the Plainpalais bar street with cheap draft and bottled beers and a local student crowd.

name: Shakers
blurb: Club known for very strong cocktails served in shaker glasses, a big dance floor and a crowd popular with English speakers.

name: AGAS free Sunday hikes
blurb: Association running free guided hikes around Geneva every Sunday; meet at 10:00 sharp at Veyrier-Douane, end of bus 8.

name: Jardin botanique de Genève
blurb: Free botanic garden with Alpine plants and a palm house of tropical vegetation, plus a zoo in its northern part.

name: Basler Münster
blurb: Romanesque-Gothic cathedral above the Rhine; free to enter, and the tower climb for CHF 6 rewards you with a wide view.

name: Kunstmuseum Basel
blurb: Huge collection from Holbein and medieval panels to modernism, including a whole Picasso room; one ticket covers three buildings.

name: Museum Tinguely
blurb: Playful kinetic machines by Jean Tinguely in a Mario Botta building; the moving sculptures are fun for all ages.
priceText: Adults CHF 18; reduced CHF 12; groups from 12 people CHF 12 each

name: Antikenmuseum Basel
blurb: Ludwig Collection of antiquities, mostly Greek with some Egyptian and Mesopotamian pieces; open late on Thursdays and Fridays.
when: Tue, Wed, Sat, Sun 11:00-17:00; Thu, Fri 11:00-22:00

name: Brötlibar
blurb: Open-sandwich bar inside the Stadthof hotel on Barfüsserplatz with a big choice of Brötli, the Swiss open sandwich.

name: Restaurant Zum Braunen Mutz
blurb: Traditional beer hall serving bratwurst with rösti, the local classic, in a no-frills setting; a good place to mix with locals.

name: Verso
blurb: Student-run bar in the university cellar, open Thursday evenings during term; cheap drinks, friendly people and live acts.
when: Thursday evenings during the university lecture period

name: Hinterhof
blurb: Bar and dance venue with a rooftop, live acts and exhibitions; open since 2011, with frequent parties and no entry fee.
priceText: Frequent parties with no entry fee

name: Basel Rhine ferry
blurb: Iconic Rhine ferry crossing that takes only two or three minutes; the view is best on a sunny day.

name: Winter ice rinks: Eglisee and Margarethenpark
blurb: Outdoor rinks open in winter, including Eglisee, on the grounds of the pool of that name, and the Margarethenpark rink.

name: Hallgrímskirkja church tower
blurb: Hilltop church with a tower and a wide view over Reykjavík; the Leif Eriksson statue stands out front.
priceText: Tower: adults 1300 kr, students 1000 kr, children (7-14) 200 kr

name: National Museum of Iceland
blurb: Walks you through the nation's history from the first settlers to today; a good background before exploring the rest of the island.
priceText: Adults 3,300 kr; students and seniors 1,600 kr; under 18 and disabled visitors free

name: Reykjavík Art Museum - Hafnarhús
blurb: Harbourside art museum with rotating shows of Erró and changing Icelandic artists; one ticket covers three art museums.
priceText: Adults 2200 kr, students 1370 kr, under 18 free; covers Hafnarhús, Kjarvalsstaðir and Ásmundarsafn

name: 871±2 Settlement Exhibition
blurb: Interactive exhibition built around Iceland's oldest archaeological ruins, dating to about 870; a quick, cheap look at the first settlers.

name: Bæjarins beztu pylsur
blurb: Reykjavík's famous hot dog stand, open round the clock; the queues say it all, and a hot dog is cheap compared with most meals.

name: Sægreifinn
blurb: Very authentic harbour seafood counter known for lobster soup, with grilled cod, shrimp and salmon; from about 800 kr a dish.

name: Ölstofa Kormáks og Skjaldar (Ölstofan)
blurb: Small, cosy, very popular bar decorated like an Icelandic grandmother's living room, with its own house beer.

name: Kaffibarinn
blurb: Club in a red two-storey timber house since the 1980s; a long-running favourite for dancing and late nights.

name: Laugardalslaug
blurb: Reykjavík's largest pool complex: hot pots, a seawater bath, a steam room and a water slide; a cheap, warming winter treat.

name: Grótta island
blurb: Small island at the western tip of the peninsula, reachable on foot at low tide; a quiet walk. Check tide times first.
when: Open most of the year; closed 1 May-15 Jul

name: Sagrada Família
blurb: Gaudí's unfinished basilica, a must-see for its tree-like columns and coloured light; the towers cost extra.
priceText: Adult basic ticket €26 (audio guide app included); under-30s and student card €24; seniors €21; towers extra

name: Museu Picasso
blurb: Strong on Picasso's early years, in a row of Gothic palaces on Carrer Montcada; the Thursday evening entry is free.

name: Palau Güell
blurb: Gaudí's early palace for industrialist Eusebi Güell, with a basement and three floors; the audio guide is included.

name: Barcelona Pavilion
blurb: Mies van der Rohe's landmark 1929 pavilion, rebuilt on its original site; a short, calm visit with a student rate.

name: La Boqueria market
blurb: Famous covered market on Las Ramblas with fresh fruit, juice stalls and ready-to-eat dishes; cheaper stalls are at the back.

name: Can Culleretes
blurb: Founded in 1786, one of Spain's oldest restaurants, serving traditional Catalan food at mid-range prices.

name: Razzmatazz
blurb: Large club with several rooms, each playing a different style from pop and retro to house and trance; worth the entry fee.

name: Club Sauvage
blurb: Former sidecar factory in Casc Antic with live music several nights a week and DJ sessions every night until about 5am.
when: Live music 22:00-00:30 (4-5 nights); DJs nightly to about 05:00

name: Free walking tours from Travel Bar
blurb: Daily free walking tours run by this bar and led by long-term expat residents; a friendly way to meet other travellers.

name: Parc del Laberint d'Horta
blurb: Hedge labyrinth in a quiet hillside park with a waterfall and canals; cheap, and free on Wednesdays.
